title: Build a Timetastic alternative with Claude: free time-off tracker spec, 32/32 checks passed
description:
Claude built a Timetastic alternative from one Markdown spec: all 32 acceptance checks passed in a real browser, along with 71 automated tests.
The test build also exposed 7 gaps in the spec, and every one is now fixed.

We gave Claude one Markdown spec for a time-off tracker for teams of 5 to 100 people and had it build the tool in four phases: people, teams, leave types and holidays; requests, balances and approvals; Who's out, the team calendar and notifications; and year end, CSV export and a calendar feed. The core rule: every day has a morning and an afternoon, days the person doesn't work and public holidays are never charged, and balances are computed from the requests every time, so they can't drift. The gaps included Admin allowances writing rows when someone merely viewed last year (which then blocked closing the current year), a team calendar that didn't say whether a holiday or a day off wins, and a pending request that had started with nowhere to appear on Who's out. What passed, what broke, what we didn't test, and when Timetastic is still the better buy.
